# Incident Report — Network Forensic Analysis
**Case:** mta-2024-07-30 | **Evidence:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 frames, ~11.3 MB, capture span 2024-07-30 06:38:48–06:48:34 +0400, ~586 sec)
**Evidence inventory:** Only the PCAP was provided; no separate IDS/Suricata alert export exists in the evidence directory.

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **172.16.1.66** | LAN scope 172.16.1.0/24; gateway 172.16.1.1 |
| MAC address | **00:1e:64:ec:f3:08** | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4`/`arp.src.hw_mac`) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-SKBR25F** | NBNS name registration, DHCP/DNS (`DESKTOP-SKBR25F.wiresharkworkshop.online`), NTLMSSP auth hostname, SMB Browser announcements |
| Domain | wiresharkworkshop.online (AD domain; DC = WIRESHARK-WS-DC at 172.16.1.4, MAC 5c:f9:dd:8c:97:35) | DNS SRV records, LDAP/Kerberos traffic |
| Logged-in user | **ccollier** | Kerberos `CNameString` (AS-REQ/TGS-REQ from 172.16.1.66) — and independently confirmed inside the malware's own C2 beacon payload (see below) |

## 2. Malware Family

**STRRAT** — a Java-based remote access trojan.

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The infected host's C2 traffic to `141.98.10.79:12132` is a plaintext, non-TLS TCP protocol. Every beacon literally self-identifies the malware:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender||1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>
```

Field breakdown observed in the capture: command=`ping`, family=`STRRAT`, bot/campaign ID=`1BE8292C`, hostname=`DESKTOP-SKBR25F`, user=`ccollier`, OS=`Microsoft Windows 11 Pro 64-bit`, AV=`Windows Defender`, STRRAT client version=`1.6`, geo=`US:United States`, uptime counter. Later beacons (from ~t+295s onward) add a base64 field `UHJvZ3JhbSBNYW5hZ2Vy` which decodes to `Program Manager` (active window title), a known STRRAT telemetry field.

This is TCP stream 83 (172.16.1.66:49754 ↔ 141.98.10.79:12132). 102 `ping` beacons were observed at a steady ~5-second interval, running continuously from t=76.99s to the end of the capture (~t=585.66s) — no other message types were exchanged on this stream.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

### Command-and-control
| Indicator | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **141.98.10.79:12132** | C2 IP:port | Plaintext TCP, hardcoded — no DNS query to this IP appears anywhere in the capture, meaning the C2 address is embedded in the STRRAT client config. 508+ seconds of continuous `ping` beaconing confirmed. |
| Bot ID `1BE8292C` | Campaign/build identifier | From beacon payload |

### Malicious domains / URLs
None. No DNS query in the capture resolves to 141.98.10.79, and no HTTP/TLS traffic carries a hostname associated with the C2. All resolved domains in the capture (Microsoft/Windows telemetry, MSN, Bing, Office, github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, repo1.maven.org, javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com, ip-api.com, wiresharkworkshop.online AD SRV records) are legitimate infrastructure — see Context section below.

### Transferred files / hashes
None extractable. All bulk data transfer in this capture is TLS-encrypted (1,427 TLS frames, ~1.46 MB) or benign plaintext HTTP (`connecttest.txt`, ip-api `/json/` response — both exported and confirmed non-malicious via `--export-objects`). No cleartext file transfer carrying an executable/JAR payload was present in the capture window, so no SHA256 can be grounded in this evidence. The STRRAT JAR's initial delivery (e.g., malspam attachment) occurred **before** this capture began.

## 4. Context (benign, not indicators)

- `ip-api.com` (208.95.112.1) `/json/` GET at t=77.9s returned the network's public-IP geolocation (Austin, TX / Google Fiber ISP) in cleartext HTTP, occurring almost simultaneously with the first C2 beacon — consistent with STRRAT's environment-fingerprinting behavior, but the endpoint itself is a legitimate public geolocation service, not attacker infrastructure.
- Large TLS sessions to `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209, ~8.7 MB in 5.8s) and `objects.githubusercontent.com` (185.199.110.133, ~828 KB) around t=64–74s could not be attributed to the infection chain — traffic is TLS-encrypted with no visible file path, and both are legitimate CDN endpoints commonly seen on developer workstations. Not reported as IOCs.
- DCERPC/SAMR and LDAP/Kerberos traffic between 172.16.1.66 and the domain controller (172.16.1.4) is standard Windows AD authentication/logon activity, not evidence of attacker-driven lateral movement or recon.
- `javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com` (Java runtime CDN) contacted at t≈340s — plausible legitimate Java update check, no causal link established to the infection.

## 5. Summary

The Windows 11 workstation **DESKTOP-SKBR25F** (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as domain user **ccollier**, is actively compromised by **STRRAT** (client v1.6, bot ID 1BE8292C). The malware beacons every ~5 seconds in cleartext to **141.98.10.79:12132**, self-reporting host identity, OS, AV product, and active window title to the operator. Attribution is signature-confirmed directly from the malware's own protocol strings, not inferred from behavior alone. The pre-capture delivery vector (how the STRRAT JAR arrived on the host) is not visible in this evidence window.
